newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire bars eight foreign reporters from Lubumbashi.
newsitem.headline: Zaire bars eight foreign reporters from Lubumbashi.

text.p: Eight foreign journalists were held at the airport in Zaire's rebel-targeted southern city of Lubumbashi overnight and expelled to the capital Kinshasa on Friday, the journalists said.

The reporters and photographers included correspondents from Radio France Internationale, the French daily Liberation, the U.S. agency Associated Press, the Independent of London and Johannesburg's Sunday Times.

"There was no explanation for our expulsion given by the authorities," Jean-Jacques Louarne, regional correspondent for Radio France Internationale, told Reuters. "All our papers were in order. Evidently they do not want journalists there."
Lubumbashi is Zaire's copper mining capital. It has been slowly encircled by rebels who say it is their next target after capturing a quarter of Zairean territory since October.
The journalists were expelled on the same day more rebel advances were reported.
Several other journalists have been expelled from the city in recent weeks, however most had failed to acquire the relevant authorisation from the government in Kinshasa.
There are several foreign journalists in Lubumbashi, who have been called to see the SNIP security police for questioning several times but have otherwise been left alone.
